question: The Chagos Archipelago Sovereignty Agreement was signed between which of the following two countries in May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**United Kingdom and Mauritius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chagos Archipelago Sovereignty Agreement** was signed between the **United Kingdom** and **Mauritius** in **May 2025**, marking a historic resolution to a longstanding territorial dispute.
 
• The agreement acknowledges **Mauritius' sovereignty** over the Chagos Archipelago, which had been under British control since **1965**.
 
• This agreement follows the **2019 advisory opinion** by the **International Court of Justice (ICJ)**, which stated that the UK's administration of the Chagos Islands was **illegal** and recommended returning the territory to Mauritius.
 
• The Chagos Archipelago is strategically located in the **Indian Ocean**, consisting of over 55 islands, with **Diego Garcia** being the most prominent island, hosting a major US military base.
 
• Under the agreement, Mauritius has agreed to recognize the continued operation of the military base on Diego Garcia by the US, ensuring mutual security interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The Chagos Archipelago was separated from Mauritius in **1965** when Mauritius was still a British colony. This separation was part of a deal in which Mauritius received financial compensation in return for the detachment of the islands.
 
• The UK then established the British Indian Ocean Territory (BIOT) and leased Diego Garcia to the **United States** for the establishment of a military base.
 
• The displacement of the native Chagossians occurred during the late 1960s and early 1970s, sparking legal and human rights controversies.
 
 
 
• **International Court of Justice (ICJ) Advisory Opinion (2019):**
 
 
• The ICJ ruled that the UK's continued administration of the Chagos Archipelago was **illegal** and that it must return the islands to Mauritius as part of the process of decolonization.
 
• The ruling, though advisory, placed significant international pressure on the UK to resolve the issue.
 
 
 
• **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) Resolution:**
 
 
• In **2019**, the UNGA overwhelmingly passed a resolution supporting the ICJ's advisory opinion and called for the UK to withdraw from the Chagos Archipelago.
 
• 120 countries voted in favor of the resolution, while only 6, including the UK and the US, opposed it.
 
 
 
• **Diego Garcia Military Base:**
 
 
• Diego Garcia remains a strategically important location for global military operations, particularly for the United States.
 
• As part of the agreement, Mauritius has committed to allowing the continued operation of the base, ensuring **regional and global security**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Agreement:**
 
 
• The sovereignty agreement is a major step towards rectifying historical injustices and addressing the grievances of displaced Chagossians.
 
• It also strengthens diplomatic ties between the UK and Mauritius, fostering cooperation in areas such as security, trade, and environmental conservation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chagossian Displacement:**

 
 
• Approximately **1,500 Chagossians** were forcibly removed from the islands to make way for the Diego Garcia base. Many were relocated to Mauritius and Seychelles.
 
• The agreement includes provisions for **compensation and resettlement** for the displaced Chagossian community, addressing a long-standing demand for justice.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Conservation:**
 
 
• The Chagos Archipelago is home to some of the world's most pristine coral reefs and marine ecosystems.
 
• The agreement includes a commitment to **protect and conserve** the ecological integrity of the islands and surrounding waters.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Located in the **Indian Ocean**, the Chagos Archipelago serves as a critical hub for monitoring and securing maritime routes.
 
• Its geopolitical importance has made it a focal point for international diplomacy and security considerations.
